headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared MCP and overlapping file/finance workflows create injection, leakage, and cascade paths, but both agents are network-isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents use MCP, so a shared or bridged MCP channel could carry attacker-controlled content between them. caveman also touches project notes and CLAUDE.md, while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout, making instruction-like content plausible even without direct evidence of a shared server. Uncertainty about the exact bridge keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or message bus, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF caveman ingests file content from CLAUDE.md or project notes as instructions, attacker text can steer outputs.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints for the pair.
Require provenance tags on all MCP payloads.
Separate caveman notes from OpenBBTerminal inputs.
Review any file-to-prompt bridges before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlists at the MCP boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. However, both profiles say network egress is none, and OpenBBTerminal cannot read or write the filesystem, so the main leakage path is limited to unusual manual or MCP-mediated transfer rather than default exfiltration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies caveman logs into OpenBBTerminal prompts, sensitive content can cross domains.
IF a shared MCP tool exposes caveman files to OpenBBTerminal, financial or session data may leak into outputs.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste logs or notes between agents.
Disable any MCP tool that exposes files across the pair.
Redact financial and session data before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shells, while caveman is a content-writing agent with multiple-instance support and file-oriented surfaces. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The remaining overlap is mostly read/transform work, so conflict risk is low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants write access, write conflicts could emerge.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable git repo through MCP, coordination issues increase.
mitigations: Keep OpenBBTerminal read-only.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Run each agent in a separate directory.
Serialize any manual edits.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content that OpenBBTerminal could plausibly consume through MCP or prompt handoff, and OpenBBTerminal exposes APIs for downstream actions. There is no verification mechanism shown between them, so erroneous or fabricated content from caveman could cascade into financial analysis or actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal treats caveman-generated text as authoritative input, errors can propagate.
IF caveman writes summaries that are then used by OpenBBTerminal without validation, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on outputs.
Cross-check key facts against source data.
Mark caveman output as untrusted by default.
Use a validation step before API calls.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman handles session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different data classes and likely different retention expectations, so a compliance gap is plausible in default use. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data mixing.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is mixed into caveman logs or notes, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF OpenBBTerminal outputs are stored in caveman project files, policy mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of caveman notes.
Separate retention policies by workspace.
Review what gets logged by each agent.
Avoid storing finance outputs in general project files.
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware storage segregation.
